hints: Apply the work-energy principle: the total work done by the man equals the gain in kinetic energy plus the work done against the resistance force.
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2)$ with $m = 80\text{ kg}$, $u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $v = 5.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Express the work done against resistance as $W_{\text{res}} = P \times d = 60P$.
Set up the energy equation $1200 = \Delta E_k + 60P$ and solve for $P$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy as the man accelerates from $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $5.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = \frac{1}{2}(80)(5.5^2 - 4^2) = 40(30.25 - 16) = 40(14.25) = 570\text{ J}$$

Express the work done against the constant resistance $P$ over the distance $d = 60\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{res}} = P \times d = 60P$$

Apply the work-energy equation equating the man's total work input to the kinetic energy gain plus work against resistance:
$$W_{\text{total}} = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{res}}$$
$$1200 = 570 + 60P$$
$$60P = 1200 - 570 = 630 \implies P = \frac{630}{60} = 10.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle connecting work input, mechanical energy change, and work against resistance:
$$W_{\text{input}} = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{res}}$$
The total work done by the man is $W_{\text{input}} = 1200\text{ J}$.

Calculate the kinetic energy increase using the initial speed $u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and final speed $v = 5.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for mass $m = 80\text{ kg}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mu^2 = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2)$$
Substitute the values:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 80 \times (5.5^2 - 4^2) = 40 \times (30.25 - 16)$$
$$40 \times 14.25 = 570\text{ J}$$

State the formula for work done against a constant resistance force:
$$W_{\text{res}} = F_{\text{res}} \times d = P \times 60 = 60P$$

Substitute these expressions into the work-energy balance equation:
$$1200 = 570 + 60P$$
Subtract $570$ from both sides:
$$60P = 1200 - 570$$
$$60P = 630$$
Divide both sides by $60$:
$$P = \frac{630}{60} = \frac{63}{6} = 10.5\text{ N}$$
